S84.03.note: The choice is stored separately for Local and Cloud mode (appearance/index.tsx picks the store by app mode), so check the choice in the mode you are in.
steps: Open the side menu and tap Settings.
Under Device, tap Appearance.
Tap Dark. The screen and app colours should switch to dark.
Tap Light, then System. Each tap should move the selected tick and change the colours to match.
Close the app completely, reopen it, and open Appearance again. The last choice should still be selected.
S84.03.where: Settings > Device > Appearance (open Settings from the side menu, then tap Appearance)

S84.04.note: The accent is not applied while the system high-contrast setting is on (apps/mobile/src/ui/theme/useTheme.ts line 34), and the screen shows no notice of that; Neutral is the default.
steps: Open the side menu and tap Settings.
Under Device, tap Accent Color.
Tap Blue. A tick should appear on Blue.
Go back and look at selected controls and highlights. They should use the blue accent.
Tap Neutral to return to the default and check the colours go back.
S84.04.where: Settings > Device > Accent Color (open Settings from the side menu, then tap Accent Color)

S84.10.needs: a Free account can pick free models; a paid account is needed for paid models
S84.10.note: The Models screen has no 'default' wording; the tap sets the one selected model (models.tsx setModel). That new chats start with it was not confirmed in the code.
steps: Open the side menu and tap Settings.
Under Device, tap General.
Tap Models. The row on General shows the current model name.
Tap a different model name in the list (a model that cannot be picked opens the model picker instead).
Go back to General and read the Models row, then start a new chat and check the model shown there matches.
S84.10.where: Settings > Device > General > Models (then tap a model name)

S84.11.needs: a model that offers effort levels
S84.11.note: The slider is shown only when the selected model has effort steps (general/index.tsx line 156); whether a new turn uses the saved value was not traced past the store.
steps: Open the side menu and tap Settings.
Under Device, tap General.
Find the Default effort slider. If it is missing, the selected model has no effort steps, so choose a model with reasoning first on the Models row.
Drag the Default effort slider to another step.
Leave the screen, come back, and check the slider stays on the new step.

Searched apps/mobile for AGENT_MODE_LABEL, 'Ask before edits', 'Edit automatically', useScopedMode and setProjectDefault.

S84.17.needs: a real phone with haptics (a simulator will not vibrate)
S84.17.note: Haptics are gated in apps/mobile/src/shared/utils/haptics.ts, useCopyAction.ts and ApprovalModal.tsx; the exact visible label of the copy control was not verified.
steps: Open the side menu and tap Settings.
Under Device, tap General.
Turn the Haptic Feedback switch off.
On a phone with haptics, copy a chat reply with its copy control, or trigger an approval prompt, and feel for a vibration. There should be none.
Turn Haptic Feedback on and repeat the same action. A short vibration should be felt.

S84.18.needs: none; a device that has allowed notifications for push
S84.18.note: Only push can be switched in the app. Email shows 'On the web' and cannot be changed here, and no in-app or browser channel switch was found on the category screen.
steps: Open the side menu and tap Settings.
Under Device, tap Notifications.
Under Notification Types, tap a category such as Chat replies.
Read the Push notifications switch and the Email notifications row under Delivery channels.
Turn Push notifications off, go back, and check the category now shows Off.
S84.18.where: Settings > Device > Notifications > Notification Types > Chat replies > Push notifications (switch)

S84.19.note: The app's own reminder says 'This is a reminder, not a lock' (TimeFocusReminder.tsx), and the screen footnote says agent failures and approvals still come through. Whether notifications are actually held on the server was not verified.
steps: Open the side menu and tap Settings.
Under Device, tap Time and focus.
Turn on Enable quiet hours.
Tap a day chip to choose days, then set Quiet Hours Start and Quiet Hours End times.
Go back to Notifications and check the Quiet hours row now reads On. Then check the held-notification behaviour against the note on this screen.
S84.19.where: Settings > Device > Time and focus > Enable quiet hours (or Settings > Device > Notifications > Quiet hours row, which opens Time and focus)
